claims.text: Increasing grain-boundary density in ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi facilitates rapid diffusion of Cr and other passivating elements.
Rapid diffusion of passivating elements enables immediate re-passivation of a worn CoCrFeMnNi surface.
Grain-boundary-assisted re-passivation governs simultaneous wear and corrosion resistance in CoCrFeMnNi.
High-pressure torsion can refine CoCrFeMnNi to a submicrometer grain size.
Annealing at 600 °C for 30 minutes after HPT optimizes the engineered grain-boundary network.
Engineered grain boundaries act as fast diffusion pathways for passivating elements, particularly Cr.
Higher grain-boundary density enhances Cr transport to the surface during and after mechanical wear.
Rapid delivery of Cr promotes immediate re-formation of a protective oxide film.
Faster re-passivation reduces both wear and corrosion.
Grain refinement increases the surface hardness of CoCrFeMnNi.
The increased hardness associated with grain refinement reduces mechanical abrasion.
Under the specified tribocorrosion conditions, ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi will have lower wear-track depths than the coarse-grained baseline.
Under the specified tribocorrosion conditions, ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi will have lower corrosion-current densities than the coarse-grained baseline.
The benefit of grain refinement will be greatest when mechanical wear repeatedly removes the passive film.
Benefits from grain refinement may be less evident under isolated wear-only or corrosion-only conditions than under simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The predicted enhancement should hold where re-passivation kinetics dominate degradation.
At sufficiently high corrosive aggressiveness or mechanical loading, grain boundaries may accelerate intergranular corrosion or re-passivation may become too slow to maintain protection.
